title: Can You FaceTime Santa? A Parent’s Guide | Dial Santa
description: Looking to FaceTime Santa? Learn how live Santa video calls work, how they differ from Apple FaceTime, and what to check before your child calls.
heading: Can you FaceTime Santa?
intro: You want the part that matters: your child asks a question, Santa hears it, and he answers. Here’s how to find that kind of Santa video call—and what to know before you start.
body:
A Santa video call, on your iPhone

People often say “FaceTime Santa” when they mean a face-to-face video conversation with Santa. Dial Santa offers a live, two-way conversation with an AI Santa in its own iPhone app. It does not use Apple’s FaceTime service, and you do not need Santa’s phone number or email address.

There is no public Santa FaceTime number provided by Dial Santa. To use the app, a parent downloads it from the App Store, sets up the account and profile, chooses call minutes, and starts a call inside Dial Santa.

What kind of Santa call are you looking for?

Three different ways to bring Santa into your home
ExperienceWhat happensWhat to check
Prerecorded messageA prepared video or phone message plays.Which details are personalized, and whether your child can actually ask questions.
Live performerA human performer talks to your family during a booked appointment.Availability, booking terms, duration, price and the video service used.
Live AI conversationAn AI character responds to what your child says in the moment.Adult supervision, voice-data handling, device support and call-minute pricing.

Dial Santa is the third option. Its Santa is an AI character, not a human performer. It is designed for a parent or guardian to set up and enjoy with their child.

How a Dial Santa call works

  1. Download on iPhone. The app requires iOS 17 or later and an internet connection.
  2. Set up as the grown-up. Verify your email and read the app’s linked policies. Add a first name and, if you choose, a wish or a good deed.
  3. Choose minutes. The download is free; calls use purchased minutes. The five-minute pack is US$2.99 in the US App Store. Local prices may vary.
  4. Get comfortable together. Start the call inside the app and let your child ask a question. Santa responds to their voice; the camera is a self-view that stays on the device.

For a fuller setup checklist, see how to call Santa.

Is FaceTiming Santa free?

Different Santa services have different prices. Dial Santa is free to download, but its live calls require paid minutes through Apple in-app purchases. Packs are 5 minutes for US$2.99, 12 for US$5.99 or 30 for US$15.99. There is no subscription, and unused minutes never expire. Check the price shown in your App Store before buying.

Will Santa see my child?

In Dial Santa, Santa responds to speech and the details a parent provides. The camera is a local self-view; it is not sent to the AI providers or our servers. Call audio and personalization are processed by service providers as described in the privacy policy. Avoid sharing addresses, school names or other details you do not want processed.

Make the first conversation easy

Have one question ready: “What do the reindeer eat?” is easier to start with than a long list. Keep the room quiet, stay beside your child, and let them take their time. A child who only wants to listen can enjoy a short hello; there is no need to push them to perform.

Try our questions to ask Santa or read the parents’ guide before the call.

FaceTime is a trademark of Apple Inc. Dial Santa is an independent app and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple.

title: How to Call Santa on iPhone: Setup, Cost & Tips | Dial Santa
description: A practical guide to calling Santa with Dial Santa: parent setup, iPhone requirements, minute packs, privacy and simple tips for your first live AI call.
heading: How to call Santa on your iPhone
intro: A quiet corner, one good question, and a grown-up nearby. Here’s how to get ready for your family’s first live AI Santa conversation with Dial Santa.
body:
First, choose the kind of call

A Santa hotline, a prerecorded message, an appointment with a human performer and a live AI video call are different experiences. Dial Santa is a live AI conversation: your child speaks and the character responds in the moment. It happens inside the iPhone app, not by dialing a telephone number or using Apple FaceTime.

What you need

  • An iPhone running iOS 17 or later and a reliable internet connection.
  • A parent or guardian to create the account, choose purchases and stay with the child.
  • Access to the parent’s email for sign-in verification.
  • Purchased call minutes and permission to use the microphone.

1. Download Dial Santa

Use the official Dial Santa App Store listing. Downloading the app is free. Calls require minutes bought inside the app through Apple; downloading alone does not start a subscription.

2. Set up the parent account

Follow the email verification steps in the app and read the linked privacy policy and terms. A parent handles setup. The app’s parental gate protects purchases and settings, but it does not replace adult supervision during a conversation.

3. Add a few personal touches

Enter a first name. You can also add a wish or a good deed, such as helping a sibling or learning something new. You do not need to write a script. Share only details you are comfortable having processed for the call; avoid a home address, school name or sensitive family information.

4. Choose your minutes and character

US minute packs are 5 minutes for US$2.99, 12 for US$5.99 and 30 for US$15.99. Local App Store prices may vary. Minutes never expire, and there is no subscription. Santa is included; Mrs. Claus and Comet each require a separate US$0.99 character unlock in the US, plus purchased call minutes.

Santa and Mrs. Claus calls can last up to six minutes each; Comet calls can last up to three. Your available balance can make the call shorter. Minutes are metered by the connected second, so unused time stays in your account.

5. Start the conversation together

Find a quiet spot, turn up the volume, and allow the microphone when the app asks. Choose the character and start the call. Santa hears and responds to speech. The camera view lets your family see themselves on the device; it is not sent to our servers or the AI providers.

Begin with a simple hello. If your child goes quiet, you can help with “We were wondering how the reindeer get ready for Christmas.” Follow the child’s pace and end the call whenever you need to.

Before buying a bigger minute pack

Try a short conversation first so you can judge the experience for your family. Santa and Mrs. Claus support English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese and Russian. Comet currently speaks English.

If the call will not connect

  • Check the internet connection and the app’s microphone permission in iPhone Settings.
  • Confirm there are minutes available and that the selected character is unlocked.
  • If you cannot hear the character, check volume and the audio device your iPhone is using.
  • If the problem continues, use Dial Santa support. Describe the issue and approximate time without sending child recordings or sign-in codes.

Recording and privacy

Recording is optional and off by default. On supported calls, you can record locally and choose whether to save the video to Photos. Provider processing of call audio and transcripts is separate from that local recording feature. Read the privacy policy for recipients, retention and deletion limits.

For conversation ideas, explore questions to ask Santa. Wondering about FaceTime? Our Santa video-call comparison explains the difference.

title: 24 Questions to Ask Santa on a Video Call | Dial Santa
description: Help your child start a Santa conversation with 24 playful questions about reindeer, the North Pole and Christmas, plus tips for shy first-time callers.
heading: 24 questions to ask Santa
intro: The best question is the one your child is curious about. Keep a few of these nearby for the moment they look at Santa and forget everything they wanted to say.
body:
For an easy first hello

  1. What have you been doing today?
  2. What is your favorite kind of cookie?
  3. Is it snowing at the North Pole?
  4. What makes you laugh?
  5. Do you have a favorite Christmas song?
  6. What do you do when you need a rest?

For little reindeer experts

  1. What do the reindeer eat for breakfast?
  2. How do the reindeer practice flying?
  3. Which reindeer likes to play games?
  4. Do the reindeer get snow on their noses?
  5. How do you keep the reindeer warm?
  6. What happens when a reindeer sneezes?

For a peek around the North Pole

  1. What does the workshop sound like?
  2. What do the elves do on their days off?
  3. Who helps you check the sleigh?
  4. Does Mrs. Claus have a favorite recipe?
  5. What is the funniest thing that happened in the workshop?
  6. If I visited the North Pole, what would you show me first?

For wishes, kindness and imagination

  1. What is a kind thing I could do for someone this week?
  2. Can I tell you something I learned?
  3. Would you like to hear about my favorite Christmas tradition?
  4. How do you choose a present for someone you love?
  5. What would you put in a snowman’s lunchbox?
  6. What should we say to the reindeer before you go?

When your child is shy

Let them listen first. You can ask the opening question together or let a toy “ask” it. Give them room to decide whether to speak. A short, relaxed hello is enough; there is no need to use every question or make the moment perfect.

Follow the answer, not the list

Pick one or two favorites. If Santa talks about cookies, “Who helps bake them?” is a natural next question. Leave a little space after each answer. A conversation about one wonderfully important reindeer detail can be more fun than racing through twenty-four questions.

Keep wishes pressure-free

A wish list can be part of the story without becoming a promise. Help children talk about what they enjoy, who they care about and what they have learned. In Dial Santa, the AI character is instructed not to promise specific gifts. A grown-up should stay nearby because AI replies can be imperfect.

Calling with Dial Santa

Dial Santa is an iPhone app for live, two-way conversations with an AI Santa. A parent sets up the profile and buys call minutes. The download is free; US minute packs start at US$2.99 for five minutes, with no subscription. Santa responds to voice, while the camera is a local self-view.

Read how to call Santa for setup, device requirements and pricing, or visit the parents’ guide. For how call audio is processed, see our privacy policy.
